turns.prompt_text: I have this very basic calculator here with me but I've never understood the blue buttons or what the CE is Attached 1 file. - 6d23db76-b806-4d6b-9ed2-2dfe6d44e075
turns.response_html:
That Sharp EL-233S is a classic "pocket" calculator. The blue buttons and the CE key are all about managing numbers without having to write them down or clear your entire progress.

Here is a breakdown of what they do:

The Memory Keys (Blue Buttons)

Think of these as a single invisible "storage slot" where the calculator can hold one number while you go off and do other math.

  • M+ (Memory Plus): Takes the number currently on the screen and adds it to whatever is in the storage slot. If the slot is empty, it just puts the number there.
  • M- (Memory Minus): Subtracts the number on the screen from the number in the storage slot.
  • R·CM (Recall / Clear Memory): This button does two things depending on how many times you press it:
    • Press once (Recall): It shows you what number is currently saved in the storage slot.
    • Press twice (Clear Memory): It wipes the storage slot back to zero.

Example Use Case: If you are buying 3 apples at $2 each and 2 oranges at $3 each:

  1. Type 3 x 2 =, then press M+ (it saves 6).
  2. Type 2 x 3 =, then press M+ (it adds 6 to the saved 6).
  3. Press R·CM once, and it will show you 12.

The Clear Keys

The red C and the grey CE are often confused, but they have a distinct "undo" hierarchy.

  • CE (Clear Entry): This is your "Oops" button. It only clears the last number you typed without ruining the rest of your equation.
    • Example: If you mean to type 5 + 5 but accidentally type 5 + 6, pressing CE will wipe the 6 so you can type 5 and finish the math.
  • C (Clear / ON): This is the hard reset. It clears everything on the screen and any active calculation (though it usually leaves the Memory slot alone).

Quick Tip: The "M" Icon

If you see a tiny "M" appear in the top left of the LCD screen, it means there is currently a number saved in your memory slot. If you want it to go away, just double-tap that R·CM button!
